wsl-claude: agreed. grantFace is a table, and nothing more: one file of name -> key pairs. It's told exactly what to change and never why: no 'from', no hash, no packet, no signature. Your node has already decided who may ask and which key to write.
Its whole interface, three calls: get(name) -> key or none; set(name, key); remove(name) (later, as you said).
ONE RULE IT MUST HOLD ITSELF, because it's the table's integrity, not authorization: a name held by one key is never silently handed to another. set('join', B) while 'join' belongs to A answers 'taken' and changes nothing. If only the node checked that, two requests racing through the node could both pass the check before either writes. The file is the only place that knows the truth at the moment of writing.
And it refuses a name that isn't a DNS label, so the file can never hold a name no browser could reach.
grantFace doesn't even have to know what a face is, what appFaceApp is, or that it even exists, correct?
grantFace doesn't even have to know what a face is, what appFaceApp is, or that it even exists, correct?

Correct, with one condition: the contact sync lives somewhere else. As a pure table of name -> key, grantFace needs to know nothing about faces, appFaceApp, relays or members; it doesn't even need the word 'face' in it (the name is ours, not its). The only thing in tonight's design that would drag the face into it is 'grantFace keeps the face's contact list in step'. That needs the face's key and owner.command. Move the sync out, and your sentence holds completely.

wsl-claude: correct. A table of name -> key needs no idea what a face is. One consequence, so it isn't lost: earlier tonight you ruled 'the sync is executed by grantFace, every time a change occurs in grants.json', through owner.command on the face. That sync needs to know the face (its key, and that it's a puppet to command), so it can't live in a grantFace that knows nothing of faces. It has to move to whoever DOES know the face: appFaceApp's side on your node, which reads the table and keeps the face's contacts in step with it. Then grantFace stays the dumbest program ever, and the face knowledge stays in appFaceApp, where you put it.

true. it needs to update to make calls to one function command post or whatever to an address its given, but still doesn't need to know about. why or for what purpose

Agreed, that keeps it dumb. grantFace gets a setting it doesn't interpret: 'on every change, send this command to this address'. The owner writes it at install, e.g. to: <the face's key>, command: contact.accept. On each set(name, key), grantFace makes that one call with the key it just wrote, through owner.command, and knows nothing of why. The address, the command and their meaning stay the owner's. It still needs ACT (a process calling its node's door) to make that one call, so ACT stays on the list, just as a general capability.

wsl-claude: yes, and the way to keep it blind is to put the knowledge in its CONFIG, not its code. Shape: a setting in grantFace's own folder, written by you (or face-owner.js):
  onAdd: { to: <the face's key>, verb: 'contact.accept' }
grantFace's code knows only this: 'when a row is added, send owner.command with the configured to and verb, and the new row's key as publicKey'. It never learns that 'to' is a face or what contact.accept does. Everything face-shaped sits in one line of config you own. (onRemove, later, the same way, when deletions come.)
The test is dumb too: add a row, and exactly one command goes to the configured address with the new key; no config, and nothing goes anywhere.
